full_source_claim_and_standing_assumptio: Fix a countable collection of infinite languages, its target K, a possibly contaminated enumeration, and the supplied set generator. Each A_n is infinite and contained in the intersection of a finite L_n minus the n observed inputs; eventually K is in L_n and mu_low(A_n,K)>=rho. In the nontrivial proof branch rho>0, with rho in [0,1] in the setup; the set generator generates in the limit. In increasing canonical target order ell_1,ell_2,..., Algorithm8 outputs w_n, the least element of A_(k(n)) avoiding current samples and prior outputs. Its m_n is the smallest positive simultaneous eventual density-rate threshold with slack 1+2^(-n), then raised to max(m_n,m_(n-1)+1). Its k(n) is the greatest 1<=k<=n with m_k/(1+2^(-k))<=2*n/rho, fallback1. Claim6.17: there exists n_star, depending on the fixed instance, such that for every n>=n_star, w_n belongs to the first ceil(2*n*(1+2^(-k(n)))/rho) elements of K. This includes target membership. Density uses canonical target prefixes, the normal input enumeration has no repetitions, and this conditional conversion has no numerical noise/omission/displacement bound. The known collection may be queried through the required density/rate and membership access, with no target-as-target or future-input query. Rho is known; no uniform threshold or runtime bound is asserted.
